question: The Slovakian newspaper The Standard1 has published an article stating that a project called Dragtivism 3.0 received financial support from the Erasmus+ programme even though it allegedly involves minors participating in events with sexually explicit content.
The article says that as part of the project a video containing sexually explicit content, and involving the participation of a minor, was recorded and then published on YouTube.

As standing rapporteur on the Erasmus+ programme, I wish to express my concern about: the suitability of the project’s content for the Erasmus+ programme, whose purpose is to promote education and exchanges; legal issues around the exposure of minors to explicit content; and the effectiveness of the Commission’s controls in approving and monitoring projects which receive Erasmus+ funding.
Can the Commission therefore answer the following questions: 1.
What mechanisms does it have to ensure that projects for young people are appropriate for their age and respect European values?

What measures is it taking to prevent minors from participating in projects with sexually explicit content, and how does it monitor the use of funds allocated to projects through the Erasmus+ programme?

How does it support young families through the Erasmus+ programme and how much funding has been allocated to support young people who have a family and wish to participate in an exchange through this programme?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (1.7.2024) The Erasmus+ Programme Guide1 sets clear standards for the protection, health, and safety of participants across all actions. Learning must take place in a safe environment which respects and protects the rights of all persons.

Participating organisations must have in place effective procedures to guarantee the safety, protection, and non-discrimination of the participants in their activities. As of 2024, the Programme’s set of rules regarding respect for EU values has been reinforced.

The Commission has contacted the National Agency in charge of the selection and monitoring of the project2 to ensure the above-mentioned standards are in place. The Commission has requested that the National Agency reviews the files and supporting documents, including the application form and the final report.

After revision, the National Agency confirmed that the project activities were considered appropriate and that the rules included in the grant agreement were respected, including parental consent prior to participation in the case of one participant who was 17 years old. Young people are supported by Erasmus+ in whatever family situation they are.

The Erasmus+ Programme Guide also provides guidance to promote equal opportunities and inclusion, diversity, and fairness across all actions. Moreover, since October 2023, beneficiaries are obliged to report on possible barriers to participation (including those stemming from family circumstances).
